title: Witnesses (Evangelii Nuntiandi 41)
hookLine: people today listen more to witnesses than teachers
tomorrow: what road does a whole church have to travel?

lines: THE AD, OR THE ONE WHO RAN IT?
cards: The ad says the running shoes will change your life. The coworker who actually finished the marathon says it was mostly cold mornings and blisters. Which one gets believed?
Pope Paul VI wrote a line about exactly that, about faith, in a letter called Evangelii Nuntiandi. And a neighbor tradition had said something close to it, in its own words.

teach.b: The question is old: what convinces?
Paul VI's answer, in paragraph forty-one: people today listen more willingly to witnesses than to teachers, and if they do listen to teachers, it's because they are witnesses.
So the first way of spreading the gospel, he says, is the witness of a truly Christian life.

Earlier in the same letter he paints it: a Christian, or a small group, living among others, sharing ordinary life, standing with them, quietly hopeful. Without a word, they stir up a question: why are they like this?
But he doesn't stop at silence.
In time the life needs the word: the name and teaching of Jesus, spoken out loud.
Jesus put it in the Sermon on the Mount: "So let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven." Here's a neighbor who says it too.

teach.h: WHY SAY YE THAT WHICH YE DO NOT?
teach.b: In the Qur'an, God asks believers, in Pickthall's translation: "O ye who believe! Why say ye that which ye do not?" The next verse calls it hateful to God to say what you don't do.
And Muslims call their declaration of faith the shahada, the testimony.
What's shared: words and life have to match, and the life is heard first. What's honestly different: for Paul VI, the witness points to Jesus as the good news itself, the Son of God.
Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet, not as God's Son.

how: Catholics often speak of evangelizing first by example, in family, work and friendship, with words ready when someone asks.

o: people whose lives show the gospel before words do
people who saw Jesus rise from the dead in person
people who sign a church record at a wedding

p: the witness of a Christian life
why say ye that which ye do not?

s: Evangelii Nuntiandi says words don't matter, only example
in time the life needs the word: the name and teaching of Jesus, spoken.
Paul VI said people listen to teachers if they are witnesses
the Qur'an asks believers why they say what they do not do

games.q: a new coach gives great speeches about teamwork but skips every practice. by Evangelii Nuntiandi 41, why has the team stopped listening?
o: players never listen to coaches anyway.
the speeches just need better arguments.
teachers get heard when they're witnesses.
games.why: Paul VI wrote that people listen more willingly to witnesses than to teachers, and to teachers because they are witnesses. the life gets heard first.

practice: Find one thing nearby that someone gave you or taught you to use: a rosary, a recipe card, a tool, a book. Look at it and remember the person, how they lived more than what they said. Let that life fill the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Witnesses. Evangelii Nuntiandi 41: people listen more to witnesses than to teachers, and to teachers who are witnesses.

orig.note: Greek for a witness, the New Testament word for one who testifies.

carryVoice: Your line: witnesses first. A life gets heard before a word does, online or at the kitchen table. Until tomorrow.
